title: The secret scanner's default generic-api-key rule skips any flagged value that contains a stop word (feed, dead, added, faded and ceded were measured), so the Phase 22 history scan, the phase scans and the seal scans cannot see a generic credential such as an RPC or API key whose value holds a common word; the scan proofs that plant random values (fixture-check.ts, and seal-verify.ts until 23-26) fail now and then when a draw spells one. EVM private keys are not affected: the project's evm-private-key rule reported 1000 of 1000 keys with a word inside

evidence.ref: PATH=/c/Users/jackc/AppData/Local/nvm/v22.16.0:$PATH node <scratch>/diag-public-address.js 3000 (the verified betterleaks 1.10.0 binary, extended.toml, the pass-1 flags of seal-verify.ts, git mode, 2026-11-12)
evidence.note: 3000 addresses drawn like seal-verify.ts randomHexStrong at 597d6db (entropy at least 3.65 bare and 0x forms), one per file in the rangeFixture m.log line shape after "token": 2992 reported (generic-api-key), 8 missed (0.27 percent); every missed value holds a hex-letter English word (feed four times, faded, added, dead, ceded); the 8 alone in a fresh repo were missed again 8 of 8, so the miss follows the value, not chance; their mean entropy (3.797) is above the 3.65 floor, so the entropy filter is not the cause

1000 random 64-hex keys, each with one of dead, feed, faded, added, ceded, beef, cafe, face, fade, bead written inside, on PRIVATE_KEY=0x lines: evm-private-key reported 1000 of 1000, generic-api-key 478; the project rule (extended.toml) carries no stop words, the default generic rule does
20000 addresses drawn with the 23-26 rule (entropy as before and no run of four or more letters a-f) in the same m.log shape: 20000 reported, 0 missed

evidence.ref: node <scratch>/mutants26.js 3 (23-26 continuation mutant run, mutant R17, which only adds a list entry and cannot reach the range fixture)
evidence.note: the self-test also printed FAIL range-public-address: m.log with no hit at all, the intermittent failure this finding explains; the first 23-26 executor had put a similar rate (about 1 percent) down to low entropy, and the entropy floor it added did not cover this cause
randomHexStrong at the start of the continuation: entropy test only; rangeFixture plants randomHexStrong(20) after "token" in m.log and asserts a public-address hit (range-public-address)

fixture-check.ts randomHexStrong: entropy test only; cases j, k, l, m and n plant two 64-hex values and five addresses per run that only generic-api-key can flag (lines 671-681 and 694-700), so a draw holding a stop word fails a case; the Phase 22 scanner, its configs and FIXTURES.json are frozen through Phase 23, so this file is not changed here

sub_claims.claim: scanner coverage: the default generic-api-key rule skips a value holding a stop word, so a generic credential with a common word in its value is not reported by any pass; a clean scan says nothing about such values
evidence: diag-public-address.js 3000: 8 of 8 missed values hold a hex-letter word, missed again alone
diag-keys2.js 1000: generic-api-key skipped 522 of 1000 values that each hold a word
sub_claims.status: confirmed (measured on the verified binary and config)

sub_claims.claim: money path unaffected: an EVM private key on a key-named line is reported by evm-private-key whatever words its hex spells
seal-verify.ts rangeFixture failed range-public-address now and then for this reason
evidence: diag-fixed.js 20000: 0 missed with the no-four-letter-run rule
sub_claims.status: fixed in plan 23-26 (randomHexStrong also rejects a run of four or more letters a-f; self-test case and mutant R19)

sub_claims.claim: fixture-check.ts (the Phase 22 scan proof) can fail cases j to n now and then for the same reason; it fails closed (a failed proof refuses the scan), so it can never pass a scan it should refuse
evidence: the per-value miss rate measured above (0.27 percent per address); a whole-run rate was not measured

sibling_sites_checked: Every random-value scan fixture under .planning/audit/tools at 597d6db: seal-verify.ts randomHexStrong (fixed in 23-26) and fixture-check.ts randomHexStrong (open, frozen) draw hex for generic-api-key cases; fixture-check.ts randomAlnumLower feeds the telegram-string-session case, a project rule in extended.toml with no stop words. Not measured: whether the default telegram-bot-api-token and generic-credential-uri rules also apply stop words. The history scan (AUD-SECRET-001) and every phase scan use the same configs, so the coverage limit applies to all of them.
severity_rationale: S3, capital none, graded by the 23-26 continuation executor under the operator's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 ("All the bugs are going to get fixed. The S1, 2 or whatever doesn't matter. Don't interrupt sessions to ask me about upgrading or downgrading"), without a stop. The capital-relevant secret, an EVM private key, is fully covered by the project rule (measured 1000 of 1000), so no signing key can slip through this way; what a clean scan cannot rule out is a generic credential (an RPC URL key, a third-party API key) whose value holds a common word, and the fixture failures fail closed. Misleading coverage and ops friction, not a capital path.
recommendation: Phase 29 (the scanner configs, fixture-check.ts and FIXTURES.json are frozen through Phase 23): (1) give fixture-check.ts randomHexStrong the no-four-letter-run rule seal-verify.ts got in plan 23-26 and re-prove FIXTURES.json; (2) decide, as a recorded choice, between a project rule without stop words for the credential shapes this bot uses (RPC provider keys in URLs, the GoPlus and honeypot API keys) and accepting the limit, and say which in AUD-SECRET-001's coverage note. EVM private keys need nothing. Nothing else is fixed in Phase 23.
